newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares edge upwards amid uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares edge upwards amid uncertainty.

text.p: Share prices edged up in Singapore on Tuesday, closing marginally higher.
"The upside was quite limited. There's still too much uncertainty in the market," said a dealer with a local firm.
"We're pretty range-bound at the moment," commented another.
The key Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended up 5.55 at 2,099.95, pulling back from an intraday high of 2,114.38.

A surge of interest in property stocks sparked a technical rebound on Monday -- recovering 25 of the 100 points the STII had lost since March 11 -- but U.S. and Singapore economic data could still dent the fragile index, dealers said.
"Another set of bad numbers will send the market back down again. It won't take much," lamented one local dealer.
Thin volume of 143.8 million shares was an indication that buying was speculative rather than broad based, the dealer said.

Property stocks were popular again, with DBS Land and Hongkong Land the most active counters. City Developments warrants were top of the 261-strong gains list, up Singapore $0.50 at S$10.60, but on volume of just 7,000 lots.
Tuesday's 97 losers were led by China Merchants, down Hong Kong $0.40 at HK$5.10.
